    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: BMC web login + ipmitool to read time

deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: DST toggle shifts BMC time; keep the operator's clock reference correct.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC daylight-saving control applies the Project-approved rule and UTC offset to the intended local-time display/clock surfaces, produces the expected change without corrupting SEL/audit chronology and restores the original policy.
original_method: Record current zone, DST rule, NTP and all clock/event boundaries; select one explicit supported enable/disable or rule/offset change; save it through the verified BMC UI after approval; compare UTC-normalized WebUI/API/SEL values and configuration against the expected rule; distinguish configuration-only coverage from an actual transition test; then restore and verify the original policy.
manual_activity: An engineer selects the supported zone/rule, coverage level and expected offset/transition and approves the time-policy mutation. A human uses and visually verifies the source WebUI. Automation may normalize multi-surface clocks and compare configuration/events, but cannot invent a DST rule or claim a real transition from a simple toggle.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware/WebUI identity, authorized account and documented clock/DST implementation
Source and target DST configuration: zone, enable state, offset, start/end rules, hemisphere and transition instants
Selected coverage: saved-policy/readback or controlled actual transition, with expected local/UTC behavior
Affected clock/display/log surfaces, trusted UTC reference, tolerance and settling interval
Impact approval for certificates, tokens, schedules, power actions, cluster/audit/monitoring
Pre/post event-boundary and repeated/nonexistent local-time evidence plan
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC/SEL/audit/host logs; preserve exact UTC and local timestamps across the configuration change or transition.
Do not choose arbitrary `different` DST values or alter absolute time to simulate a transition unless separately approved with a recovery plan.
Verify target, timezone, rule and expected offset before saving; do not change unrelated timezone, NTP or host clock settings.
Protect credentials and use supported readbacks; distinguish display shift, stored UTC and SEL timestamp conversion.
Stop on unknown rule, unexpected UTC change, NTP overwrite, duplicate/missing chronology beyond the documented transition or cross-surface mismatch.
Restore the original rule and verify both configuration and normalized clocks; do not retry or rewrite logs to hide chronology.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, rule/transition matrix, coverage level, affected clock surfaces, NTP/tolerance, impact and restoration before presenting the UI change.
Capture pre-change DST/zone/NTP configuration, normalized WebUI/API/SEL/reference clocks and event boundaries.
After human saves one approved change, collect UI/audit plus immediate/settled normalized reads and compare expected offset or transition behavior.
Restore and verify the original policy, preserving evidence without unrelated clock writes, log clear, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact DST rule/matrix, configuration-only versus actual-transition scope and expected UTC/local/chronology behavior.
Approve the WebUI change, NTP/time-sensitive impact, tolerance and restoration/recovery plan.
Review normalized configuration/clock/event evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Conceptually relevant but too vague: a toggle plus before/after clock does not prove which rule/transition or surfaces changed, whether UTC stayed correct, or whether repeated/nonexistent local times and audit entries behave correctly.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the verified WebUI control with one explicit Project-approved zone/rule/offset; corroborate using supported protected API/IPMI reads normalized to UTC and restore the exact baseline.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The `Change different Daylight saving time` instruction, single change Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek WebUI/readback/risk and 5/5-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not invent a universal one-hour shift.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Apply one defined DST policy change, prove saved configuration and expected normalized offset/transition on all in-scope surfaces, preserve chronology and restore the baseline.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC firmware/WebUI time implementation and Project-supported timezone/DST rule.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/WebUI/API/IPMI versions, timezone rule database and NTP/PTP configuration.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor DST/timezone semantics, Project regional time policy, IANA/rule authority if applicable and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Turns `different DST` into an explicit rule/coverage matrix with UTC normalization, event chronology and restoration while retaining the source setting action.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A saved toggle tests configuration but not necessarily a real transition; a display shift does not prove stored UTC or SEL chronology; API-only changes do not prove WebUI control.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Zone/rule/transition, scope, expected offsets, affected surfaces, NTP, evidence and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect rules can misdate audit/security events and scheduled actions; real boundary testing may require controlled time changes with greater risk.

project_override_considerations: A Project may choose configuration-only coverage or an actual transition as defined by its SPEC. UI automation is acceptable if actual WebUI save/display evidence remains. API-only overrides must record uncovered WebUI coverage. A one-hour assumption is invalid unless the approved rule states it.
expected_evidence: Target/version identity, approved zone/DST rule/transition and coverage choice, NTP/tolerance/time-sensitive impact approval
Pre-change UI configuration, normalized WebUI/API/SEL/reference clocks and unmodified event boundaries
WebUI save/audit evidence naming exact enable/rule/offset/start/end settings
Immediate/settled observed versus expected local offset or transition, UTC invariance, affected-surface and audit/SEL chronology comparison
Exact baseline restoration, no unrelated time/log mutation or retry, coverage limits and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently target DST-setting impact. They are severely under-specified but do not present competing targets or operations; Project/vendor inputs can define the actual rule and coverage.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The DST configuration objective is identifiable. Missing timezone/rule/transition and clock-surface details are execution-readiness inputs, not an irreducible permanent BLOCKED condition.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE and expands a generic toggle into an explicit rule, coverage, normalized-surface and restoration contract.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification and strengthens configuration-versus-transition distinction, ambiguous/repeated-time evidence and no universal offset assumption.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic before/after time with rule-specific UI/audit/UTC/chronology evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps timezone selection and absolute clock-setting cases separate from DST policy.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an arbitrary toggle or assumed one-hour display change from being reported as correct DST behavior and protects audit chronology while preserving the functional setting requirement.
independent_technical_reasoning: DST is a rule applied to local representation, not simply an instruction to move the underlying UTC clock. Correct behavior depends on zone, transition definitions and whether firmware timestamps SEL in UTC or local time. Therefore a valid test must name the rule and coverage level, normalize all readings, inspect chronology and restore the original policy rather than accept any observed time change.
